One-anchor calibration by held-out publication. Open points are uncalibrated RMSE and filled points calibrated RMSE, averaged over the saved random anchor selections. Red indicates increased mean RMSE. Publications are ordered by RMSE change. The overall percentage reduction is calculated from mean publication-level RMSE; its interval uses publication bootstrap resampling. Publication labels are defined in Supplementary Table S1.

Anchor-number comparison in the fixed subset supporting five anchors. A: Individual-publication percentage reductions and the percentage reduction in mean publication RMSE. The overall curve is not the mean of individual percentage reductions. Shading is a 95% publication-bootstrap interval. B: Paired calibrated RMSE with one and five anchors; red indicates higher RMSE with five. The same publications and test measurements are used. Additional anchors also change the shrinkage factor.

Retrospective calibration diagnostics. A: Mean offset and sampled range across single-anchor choices against mean uncalibrated test residual. Dashed diagonal indicates equality. Mean offsets alone do not determine mean RMSE across varying anchor choices. B-C: Sampled offset distributions for P096 and P119 across anchor counts. Boxplots and point ranges are not confidence intervals, and sampled panels are not independent experiments. Test residuals were not used to select anchors or estimate calibration offsets.
Calibration effects and 95% publication-bootstrap intervals under each curation policy. Evaluation populations and test measurements can differ between policies.
Pooled variance fractions and 95% parametric-bootstrap intervals from the intercept-only crossed random-intercept model. Intervals are marginal and their bounds do not sum to 100%.
